init.title: Voice settings
init.description:
These settings control how presses are handled and how replies are spoken. Replacing a request cannot undo actions it already performed. Simultaneous full duplex is unavailable. Stopping after transcription does not disable tools built into a live speech provider; use a transcription-only provider when actions must be disabled.

**Reply condition:** all of its conditions must pass for a reply to be spoken. They are checked once at the start of each request; leave it empty to always speak, and a condition that cannot be evaluated counts as not met. Template conditions can use the variables `speaker`, `remote` and `held`.

data_description.pipeline_id: The Assist pipeline that processes speech: speech-to-text, conversation agent and text-to-speech. A removed pipeline fails with an error instead of falling back.
data_description.mode: Transcription only stops after speech recognition and plays no reply. Execute commands runs the whole pipeline and speaks the reply on the reply speaker.
data_description.speaker: The media player that speaks replies. Used only when executing commands. Choose no spoken reply to stop the pipeline before the reply is played.
data_description.output_mode: Automatic streaming starts speaking as soon as a streamed reply is ready. Waiting for the complete reply starts later but plays a finished audio file, which avoids breakup with providers that only produce speech at about real-time pace.
data_description.stream_head_start: Delays the start of a streamed reply by this many seconds so the speaker can buffer; replies that finish sooner play at once. Raise it if streamed replies break up in the first seconds. No effect when waiting for the complete reply. 0 keeps the default behaviour.
data_description.busy_processing: What to do when the button is pressed before the previous request is answered: reject the press, keep one pending request, or replace the current request. Replacing cannot undo actions already performed.
data_description.busy_playback: What to do when the button is pressed while a reply is playing: reject the press, answer one pending request afterward, or stop the reply and start the new request.
data_description.context_mode: Reuse keeps the Home Assistant conversation so follow-ups such as 'and double that?' work. Fresh makes every press an independent conversation.
data_description.input_mode: One request per hold records until the button is released. Alternating conversation keeps listening while the button is held: speak, pause, hear the reply, then speak again. It needs a hold-to-talk remote.
data_description.remote_type: Leave on Automatic unless the remote was detected as the wrong type. Changing it reconnects the remote.
data_description.min_press_seconds: Ignores voice-button taps shorter than this, so a spurious tap never starts a request; a real hold starts this much later. 0 turns it off. Useful for a Fire TV remote that fails with "No microphone audio" right after waking: it re-sends the key that woke it as an instant tap. 0.1 s is a good starting point. Fire TV remotes only.
data_description.max_request_seconds: The longest a single request can last on any remote: a whole hold in One-request mode, and each turn in Alternating conversation. Reaching it ends the request with a capture-limit error. Lower it to stop a stuck button recording; raise it for long dictation. Remotes that are not hold-to-talk also end at about 15 seconds of speech or at silence, whichever comes first.
data_description.max_conversation_seconds: The longest a whole button hold can last in Alternating conversation mode. It is ignored in One-request mode and must not be shorter than the maximum request length.
data_description.reply_condition: Conditions that must all pass for a reply to be spoken. Checked once at the start of each request (and each turn in Alternating conversation). Leave empty to always speak. A condition that errors counts as not met. Template conditions can use the variables speaker, remote and held.

pipeline_missing.title: Assist pipeline missing for {remote}
pipeline_missing.description:
The remote **{remote}** is set to use the Assist pipeline `{pipeline}`, which no longer exists. Voice requests from this remote fail until you choose another pipeline.

Go to **Settings → Devices & services → Bluetooth Remote Voice**, open the menu of **{remote}**, choose **Configure**, and pick an existing pipeline.

speaker_missing.title: Reply speaker missing for {remote}
speaker_missing.description:
The remote **{remote}** is set to play replies on `{speaker}`, which no longer exists. Commands still run, but their spoken reply will not play.

Go to **Settings → Devices & services → Bluetooth Remote Voice**, open the menu of **{remote}**, choose **Configure**, and pick another speaker or choose none.

speaker_unavailable.title: Reply speaker not working for {remote}
speaker_unavailable.description:
Replies from the remote **{remote}** could not be played several times in a row because the speaker `{speaker}` is not working. Commands still run, but their spoken reply is lost. This notice clears when a reply plays again.

Go to **Settings → Devices & services → Bluetooth Remote Voice**, open the menu of **{remote}**, choose **Configure**, and pick another speaker or choose none.
